samples: This program builds a Markdown table from a header row and body rows. It pads every column to its widest cell, header included, and adds a dashed divider line under the header. It is pure text formatting with no input handling, and its main function only prints a small fruit-price table to the console as a demo. Rows shorter than the header are filled with blanks, but cells beyond the header's column count are dropped, so ragged input is tolerated rather than rejected.

This program turns a header row and body rows of text into a Markdown table. Each column is padded to the width of its longest cell (the header included), with a dashed divider line under the header. It is a pure formatting library whose only side effect is a demo entry point that prints a small fruit-price table to the console. Rows that are shorter than the header are filled in with blank cells, but cells in a row beyond the header's column count are silently dropped.

This program turns a table, made of a header row and any number of body rows of text, into a Markdown table string in which every column is padded to the width of its widest cell (header included), with a dashed divider line under the header. It's pure formatting logic with no outside dependencies apart from printing to the console, and its demo `main` prints a small fruit, price and stock table. Be aware that rows with fewer cells than the header are padded with blanks, while cells beyond the header's column count are silently dropped, and nothing escapes special Markdown characters like pipes in cell text.

This program builds a Markdown table from a header row and body rows, padding every column to the width of its widest cell (header included) and adding a dashed divider line under the header. Missing cells in short rows are treated as blank, and the rendering itself is pure; only the demo entry point uses the console to print a sample fruit-price table. It is a small, self-contained formatter that is easy to reuse, but it has no escaping of special characters like pipes and it measures width by simple text length, so wide or non-ASCII characters may not align perfectly.

This program turns a table, made of a header row and any number of body rows of text, into a Markdown table string where every column is padded to the width of its widest cell, with a dashed divider line under the header. Rows that are shorter than the header get blank cells, and the module is pure apart from its demo entry point, which prints a small fruit price table to the console. It is a good fit if you need simple, aligned Markdown output, but it does no escaping of special characters (such as pipes) in cells and does not handle rows longer than the header, whose extra cells are dropped.
